Evidence: Chandrababu Naidu, the TDP chief, met Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Jayalalithaa regarding the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh. He requested her to pressure the Centre to ensure that both Telangana and Seemandhra regions are taken into confidence before any bifurcation. Naidu also asked the President to call leaders from both regions to discuss the issue. Jayalalithaa supported the idea of consensus for any bifurcation. Naidu criticized the Congress party for its handling of the situation, claiming it was playing 'dirty politics' and that the issue had escalated to a national crisis (Sources 1 and 2).
Justification: The retrieved evidence confirms that Naidu met Jayalalithaa and requested the President to involve leaders from both regions in discussions about the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh. This directly supports the claim that Naidu met Jayalalithaa and asked the President to call leaders from both regions. The evidence from Sources 1 and 2 explicitly states these actions and requests made by Naidu, thus corroborating the claim.
